an3.34:1.1: This short text is surprisingly difficult to interpret exactly, but it helps to think of it as differentiating those deeds that result in rebirth from those that do not.
an3.34:2.1: The text does not use emphatic forms (“any deed”), since some deeds will yield their result in the same life. It is restricted to those deeds that result in rebirth.
an3.34:2.2: The stock phrase on the threefold manifestation of _vipāka_ (see [an6.63:36.2]()) appears superfluous here. Its purpose is normally to establish where results manifest, yet that is already established in the premise. It seems awkward, if not contradictory, to say there are three possible manifestations where the text has already spoken of just one. I suspect it is a later addition to this passage, possibly prompted by taking the passage to be a universal one, which must then account for all possibilities.
